clue.text: Mall forerunner's become tiresome

definitions.meaning: in the name of the London street ... Mall, this word comes just before Mall
to lose interest or appeal through sameness, as a routine does

explanation.surface: Something that came before the shopping mall has started to bore people.
explanation.definitionFit: Pall Mall is a famous London street, and a thing that palls grows dull or wearisome.

clue.text: It follows it might have to be taken out

definitions.meaning: the supplementary section that comes after the main text of a book

definitions.text: it might have to be taken out
definitions.meaning: the small organ off the gut that a surgeon removes when it is inflamed

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: the back-matter section of a book follows the text, and the body's vestigial organ is often surgically removed.

clue.text: Dodgy sun-baked starter removed from eatery

indicators.note: baked suggests the letters have been cooked into a new form, so they are rearranged
the opening letter is taken off the following word

parts.note: a cafe is a small eatery

explanation.surface: A warning that sunburnt food from a restaurant missing its first course could be risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baked' rearranges SUN to UNS; 'starter removed from' takes the C off CAFE to leave AFE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something dodgy is risky or dangerous, not secure.

clue.text: Bond's suspicious about Bellow

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: wary means cautious or suspicious
to rant is to shout loudly, to bellow

explanation.surface: James Bond is wary of the novelist Saul Bellow, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' and 'Bellow' look like names (the spy and the novelist) but are the definition and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee or pledge: a bond is a binding promise, as a warranty is a written assurance.

clue.text: States true version up front: 'It was one's first abode'

indicators.note: the rearranged piece is placed in front of the other piece
a version is a different rendering, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: US is the United States

explanation.surface: An American political slogan placed at the top of a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'States' looks like a verb but is the country; the definition is a riddle about where everyone lived before birth.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone lived in the womb before birth, making it each person's first home.

clue.text: Gets more friendly with expelled members

indicators.note: expelled means thrown out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: someone who warms to you becomes friendlier

explanation.surface: Someone grows friendlier towards members who have been thrown out of the club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expelled' removes W (with) from WARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbs are members of the body, an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Drive home with knickers virtually unrestrained

parts.note: to ram a point is to drive it home forcefully

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word is not quite complete and loses its final letter

parts.note: pants is the British word for knickers, underwear

explanation.surface: Someone drives home wearing so little underwear they are almost uninhibited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' drops the last letter of PANTS. In Britain pants are underwear, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something rampant spreads wildly, without check or control.

clue.text: Rating indignation as a symbolic thing?

parts.note: a rating is an ordinary sailor, and an old salt is a seasoned sailor
ire is anger or indignation

explanation.surface: A query whether giving something a score of outrage makes it symbolic.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating here is a naval seaman, not a score.
explanation.definitionFit: The diagonal cross of St Andrew on the Scottish flag is an emblem, a symbol of Scotland.

clue.text: Element of organ infection and reduced energy associated with smoker

parts.note: flu is a viral infection

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, here to just its first letter, the usual short form

parts.note: a pipe is something smoked

explanation.surface: A medical note: a heavy smoker with a chest infection has little energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the body, but the instrument is meant; 'smoker' is a pipe, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind of organ pipe that sounds like a whistle or recorder, one component of a church organ.

clue.text: Author includes 'Mountain King' as a perfume ingredient

indicators.note: includes means the outer word holds the others inside

parts.note: Kingsley or Martin Amis, English novelists
berg is a mountain, as in iceberg or the Afrikaans word
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A novelist's book features 'In the Hall of the Mountain King', apparently as a scent.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted 'Mountain King' recalls Grieg's piece but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A waxy substance from sperm whales long used as a fixative in fine perfumes.

clue.text: Turn on US president (wife getting chop)

parts.note: George Bush, either of the two presidents
to hack is to chop

explanation.surface: A call to attack an American president while his wife is being axed.
explanation.definitionFit: To ambush or suddenly attack, which is to turn on someone.

clue.text: Mark ordered to secure grand opening

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A man named Mark was told to arrange a grand launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand opening' gives just G.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge is an emblem or mark showing rank or membership.

clue.text: Health food to eat with bulk

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: bran is the husk of grain, eaten as a fibre-rich health food

explanation.surface: Advice on a nutritious diet for building up muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' puts W (with) inside BRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscular strength or sheer physical size; brawn is bulk.

clue.text: Shady stationer nursing bad back

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one word cradles the other

parts.note: read literally, one who stations or sites things: a siter

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: something bad is a sin, a wrong

explanation.surface: A dodgy shopkeeper selling paper is caring for someone with a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stationer' is not the shopkeeper but one who stations, a SITER; 'back' turns SIN to NIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something sinister is threatening or suspect, shady.

clue.text: Bird book released by bailiff

indicators.note: released by means let go, so a letter departs from the word

parts.note: beagle is an old word for a sheriff's officer or bailiff

explanation.surface: A bird kept as evidence is freed by the court official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bailiff' uses the old slang sense of beagle, a court officer; 'released by' drops the B.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bird of prey; an example of a bird.

clue.text: Enemy broadcast 'fake'!

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so the word is heard aloud

parts.note: the enemy as a body means foes

explanation.surface: Someone shouts that an opponent's broadcast is fake news.
explanation.walkthrough: French faux sounds like foes.
explanation.definitionFit: Faux, borrowed from French for false, means imitation or sham.

clue.text: Port Washington's outskirts flooded by river

indicators.note: flooded by means engulfed, so the river surrounds the other letters

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: the outskirts are the edges, so the first and last letters

explanation.surface: The edges of a port in Washington State are flooded by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Tawny is a kind of port wine, not a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawny port is a wood-aged style of fortified wine; tawny names that wine.

clue.text: Metal cruet cast a slight shade

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: cast as in throwing or moulding anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A metal condiment holder throws a faint shadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges CRUET to CTURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture is a trace or tinge, a faint hint of colour.

clue.text: Many lands

definitions.meaning: plenty, as in having lots of something
secures or claims, as when you land a good seat

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: 'bags of' means lots, and to bag something is to land or secure it.

clue.text: Live! Hit performer's jazz instrumentalist

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
one who bops, that is who hits, is a bopper

explanation.surface: A live gig by a star with a chart hit who plays jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit performer' suggests a pop star but is one who performs a hit, a bopper.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is a fast, complex style of jazz, and a musician playing it is a bebopper.

clue.text: Indications of office sin: gin-swilling one on one

indicators.note: swilling means sloshing about, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: An official's misdeed: drinking gin while working one-to-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swilling' rearranges SIN GIN to INSIGN; then I and A, both meaning one.
explanation.definitionFit: Badges or emblems marking rank or official position.

clue.text: Corrupt data etc repaired

parts.note: INF is short for information, data, as in the .inf file extension

indicators.note: repaired means fixed by rearranging

explanation.surface: Damaged computer data and the like have been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repaired' rearranges ETC to ECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrupt files or a system is to contaminate them, as a virus does.

clue.text: Shows competence when dropping first black

indicators.note: dropping first means losing the opening letter

parts.note: someone who is able shows competence, so 'is able'

explanation.surface: Someone proves capable once they stop coming last, or first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping first' removes the I from IS ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic term for the colour black.

clue.text: Record run

definitions.meaning: a disc carrying one track, released on its own
in cricket, a hit scoring one run

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: a song released alone is a single, and in cricket a single is one run.

clue.text: Cash substitute, if Kent got hit

indicators.note: hit means battered, so the letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A voucher instead of money, offered if a man named Kent got assaulted.
explanation.definitionFit: A voucher given as a present that can be exchanged for goods instead of money.

clue.text: Working to get rid of one part of the percussion section?

indicators.note: getting rid of means discarding, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a going concern is a working one
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A musician tries to sack one drummer from the orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get rid of' drops I from GOING.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuned metal disc that is struck, an example of an orchestral percussion instrument.

clue.text: See 9
A lot of money that's forced into the ground

definitions.meaning: a fortune, as in making a heap of cash
a heavy post driven into soil to support a building

explanation.definitionFit: Double definition: making a pile is getting rich, and a pile is a driven foundation post.

clue.text: It's fabulous producing old-hat student humour?

parts.note: uni, short for university, is where a student goes
corn is banal, trite humour

explanation.surface: Tired campus jokes are claimed to be wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-hat' qualifies the humour: corn is stale humour. 'fabulous' means from fable, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythical horned horse, a creature of fable and legend.

clue.text: Old Red Belly performing without bass

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters put on a show in a new order
without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: An aged band called Red Belly plays a gig with no bass player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops B to leave REDELLY, which 'performing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an elderly person is aged, old.
